correctness.rationale: An independent-from-certificate exhaustive reconstruction of both pure simplicial complexes enumerates 256 maximal acyclic Hasse matchings on the full tetrahedron and 256 on its boundary, with exact face vectors (28,300,1544,3680,3672,1600,256) and (24,216,896,1680,1152,256). The checker reconstructs the canonical embedding and verifies 3428 distinct elementary free-face removals, each with upper face maximal and unique cover, respecting the target and leaving it exactly. Four link face vectors agree and each link has 856 collapse pairs. These are complete finite proofs under the explicit definitions, not numerical extrapolation. The source and target are pure acyclic Morse matching complexes, not ordinary or generalized ones. The claimed natural inclusion simplicially collapses and is therefore a simple-homotopy equivalence.

value.rationale: A canonical embedding rather than an arbitrary equivalence is the natural question for comparing optimal discrete Morse matching parameter spaces of the simplex and its boundary. Establishing that it simplicially collapses is a structural and simple-homotopy refinement of the recently proved 81-sphere homotopy equivalence, valid for a meaningful smallest previously unsolved relative-collapse instance after the triangular case. The explicit pure-link collapse explains why the pure category behaves differently from the generalized nonacyclic category. Exact finite certificates resolve a naturally motivated question; no paper-sized general theorem or infinite-family claim is needed.
